- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows (especially 30d) when sentiment is positive or neutral, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., -1.98, -0.51), model often fails to adjust downward quickly; prices drop more sharply than forecasted.
- Overshoots after positive sentiment spikes are common — model peaks too high, then corrects too slowly.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high prices longer than observed, especially when sentiment is mixed or mildly negative.
- Forecasts for later days (e.g., 25–30d) are often too optimistic, especially if sentiment is weak or trending down.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over recent days, model may overfit to recent highs and ignore structural downward trends.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to average or smooth out sharp drops, leading to lagged corrections.
- Correction should be applied more aggressively when sentiment is negative and price is above 80.00 — model often fails to recognize imminent correction.
- Avoid over-reliance on recent 18-day history; sentiment from 3–5 days prior is more predictive of short-term correction than 18-day average.
